newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed manufacturing index off 0.1 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed manufacturing index off 0.1 pct in Jan.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago on Tuesday said its Chicago Fed Midwest Manufacturing Index (CFMMI) slipped 0.1 percent to 124.3 in January from 124.4 in December.
January's slight decline is likely to be a brief pause, given the recent spate of positive economic reports, the Chicago Fed said in a report.
Most sectors both nationally and regionally posted modest gains or declines in January, the report said.
The manufacturing component of the Federal Reserve Board's industrial production index fell 0.2 percent.
"A slowdown in the steel sector was the main reason for the Midwest's (largely) unchanged performance," the bank said.
January's steel-related activity fell 0.6 percent from the previous month, and actual raw steel production was down more than 5.0 percent from very high levels a year ago, it said.
"Much of that decline may have been due to mill outages rather than an easing in demand for steel," the report said.
Nevertheless, the CFMMI closely matched the nation in recent months, despite some downward revisions in both regional and national indexes in December, the Chicago Fed said.
